newsitem.title: UK: TUC backs away from unions' UK minimum wage demand.
newsitem.headline: TUC backs away from unions' UK minimum wage demand.

text.p: The leadership of the Trades Union Congress (TUC) will not be asking its annual conference next week to endorse a precise figure for a national minimum wage, general secretary John Monks said on Thursday.
But left-wing unions have put forward a motion calling for a future Labour government to introduce a statutory minimum of 4.26 stg an hour, and within a year of taking office.

Monks told a news conference that the TUC's general council, made up of himself and leaders of member unions, thought a minimum of four stg would be "reasonable", but it would not back any precise figure until real negotiations were about to start.
The Labour Party is committed to introducing a minimum wage, but it, too, has declined to name a figure. It will set up a commission including unions and employers to recommend a level.

TUC leaders persuaded members not to set a precise figure at last year's conference, to avoid giving ammunition to Labour's opponents, but they agreed to fix a level this time and campaign for it ahead of the next election, to be held by mid-1997.

However, Monks told the news conference that the debate was "hypothetical" without a Labour government, adding the TUC would set a figure "when we're clear about the timetable for a Low Pay Commission and if there is going to be a Low Pay Commission".
